newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia capital market raises 34.5 bln rgt in '96.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia capital market raises 34.5 bln rgt in '96.

text.p: Funds totalling 34.5 billion ringgit were raised in the Malaysian capital market in 1996, up 54 percent from 22.4 billion raised in 1995, Bank Negara said in its 1996 annual report released on Friday.
The private sector continued to be the main mobiliser of funds, raising 29.4 billion ringgit in 1996 against 19.6 billion in the previous year.
The central bank said the increase was due to more money being raised on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and increased issues of private debt securities (PDS).
New funds raised through the equity market reached a record 15.9 billion ringgit in 1996, against 11.6 billion in 1995, the bulk of which was raised through rights issues.
In the PDS market, net funds raised amounted to 13.6 billion ringgit in 1996, compared with 11.9 billion a year earlier, accounting for 46 percent of total funds tapped by the private sector.

Funds raised in the capital market were channelled mainly to the manufacturing and services sectors, particularly large infrastructure projects in transport, telecommunications and utilities, Bank Negara said.

The central bank said the increase in funds raised in the PDS market reflected the rise in net issues of bonds by the national mortgage firm, Cagamas Bhd, and the 2.2 billion ringgit issue of Islamic bonds by the new Kuala Lumpur International Airport.
In 1996, Cagamas floated 16 issues of Cagamas bonds amounting to 4.7 billion ringgit, compared with seven issues worth 3.0 billion ringgit in 1995.
Funds raised through short-term paper increased by 31.4 percent to 3.7 billion ringgit in 1996, Bank Negara said.

During the year, the Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd completed 89 corporate rating exercises of both long and short-term PDS worth 16.9 billion ringgit, compared with 93 ratings valued at 16.3 billion ringgit in 1995.

Total funds raised from the government securities market in 1996 were 6.0 billion ringgit through three issues of 2.0 billion ringgit each, up from 2.0 billion ringgit raised in 1995. Bank Negara said the new issues were mainly to meet market demand and to provide a benchmark yield curve to support the development of the domestic bond market, as the financial position of the Malaysian government remained strong.
In 1996, the share of total net funds raised in the capital market to total loans extended by the banking system increased to 51 percent from 40 percent in 1995.
